headline: Stone.js: write your app logic once for any runtime
summary: This new framework allows developers to write their application logic once and deploy it across various runtimes, including server, cloud functions, and the browser.
details: Traditional development often requires rewriting application logic for different environments like servers, serverless functions, or frontends. Stone.js aims to solve this by separating application domain logic from its execution context.

The core idea is 'Application = Domain x Context'. Developers define the domain logic once, and Stone.js applies the appropriate context (server, function, browser, agent) at runtime. This eliminates the need for multiple codebases for the same functionality.

Stone.js supports numerous adapters, including Node HTTP, AWS Lambda, Azure Functions, GCP Cloud Functions, and even edge runtimes and browsers. This ensures a single domain can run virtually anywhere.

The framework utilizes TC39 stage 3 decorators (Symbol.metadata) for defining adapters, avoiding experimental features and external dependencies like reflect-metadata. It operates exclusively with ESM.

Stone.js also introduces an MCP (Meta-Cognitive Programming) server for development. This allows AI coding agents to introspect and interact with the application, potentially streamlining development workflows.
The project is actively seeking pilot developers to test Stone.js, break it, and provide feedback. This offers a unique opportunity to influence the framework's development directly.
